messages.subject: basic questions on reading data
parts:
Dear list, sorry for basic questions. I have read through all the
links in aroma´s webpage and I have only managed to read the cdf file
in. I am not sure if I understood all the steps, so I would like to
check with you.

I am trying to find out if I can read 140 U133 plus files on my 1gb
PC, normalise them using affyPLM and then being able to perform
quality control using NUSE plots.

Do all chips have to have the same name format so that
aroma.affymetrix can read them?. Does this mean that I have to change
all 140 names manually?

I have created a working directory called HG-U133_Plus_2 and in this
directory I have two folders, one called "RawData" with all the .CEL
files and one called "annotationData" with subfolders \chipTypes\HG-
U133_Plus_2 and the cdf file in here.

Some of the .CEL files have name similar to
"07SE181HGU133Plus_2.0_210207.CEL" but others have
"AA001_1.3Plus280704.CEL". Do I have to change these names to
something like

07SE181,210207,HGU133Plus_2.CEL
and
AA001_1.3,280704,HGU133Plus_2.CEL


Do I have to change my "RawData" directory name to match my chip
names, something like "HGU133Plus_2"?

Thanks in advance for your help,

David

messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] basic questions on reading data
parts:
> I am trying to find out if I can read 140 U133 plus files on my 1gb
> PC, normalise them using affyPLM and then being able to perform
> quality control using NUSE plots.
You should be able to do all this without a problem.

> I have created a working directory called HG-U133_Plus_2 and in this
> directory I have two folders, one called "RawData" with all the .CEL
> files and one called "annotationData" with subfolders \chipTypes\HG-
> U133_Plus_2 and the cdf file in here.

First, I want to make sure you have the correct directory structure.
Suppose I have dataset with several tissue samples. All data is
located within the 'rawData' directory of the working directory. My
files are laid out in the directories as follows:

rawData/tissues/HG-U133_Plus_2/u1332plus_ivt_breast_A.CEL
rawData/tissues/HG-U133_Plus_2/u1332plus_ivt_breast_B.CEL
...

My CDF file is located in the 'annotationData' directory as follows:

annotationData/chipTypes/HG-U133_Plus_2/HG-U133_Plus_2.cdf

Is your setup *exactly* like this?

> Do all chips have to have the same name format so that
> aroma.affymetrix can read them?. Does this mean that I have to change
> all 140 names manually?

Do you mean the filenames? There are some restrictions on
filenames. I think you'll want to avoid commas, but underscores
would be fine.

> 07SE181,210207,HGU133Plus_2.CEL
> and
> AA001_1.3,280704,HGU133Plus_2.CEL

You could even just call them 07SE181.CEL and AA001_1_3.CEL if you
want. You don't need to have HGU13... in the filename, if thats what
you are asking.

> Do I have to change my "RawData" directory name to match my chip
> names, something like "HGU133Plus_2"?

Notice that in the above directory structure, the 'HG-U133_Plus_2' is
in both the annotationData and rawData directories. You will need to
match this in your setup.

Let me know how you go.

Cheers,
Mark
